items.title: Anti-Sterlite protests: CM orders ₹5.25-cr. additional relief to victims
points: Thirteen people lost their lives (in police firing) and 40 people sustained grievous injuries in the anti-Sterlite protests in Thoothukudi on May 22 and 23, 2018. | Photo Credit: N.
Joseph Vijay on Wednesday ordered disbursement of an additional ₹5.25 crore as relief to the families affected during the anti-Sterlite protest in Thoothukudi in 2018.
According to an official release, during the anti-Sterlite protest in Thoothukudi on May 22 and May 23, 2018, 13 people lost their lives (in police firing) and 40 people sustained grievous injuries.
Their families had already been provided relief of ₹25 lakh each for the 13 deceased and ₹5 lakh each for the 40 grievously injured.
Considering their request and based on the recommendations of the Justice Aruna Jagadeesan Commission of Inquiry, Mr. Vijay ordered the additional relief to the families, the release said.
Accordingly, the families of the 13 deceased persons would receive the remaining ₹25 lakh each, taking the total compensation to ₹50 lakh per family.

items.title: Low-pressure area likely to form over Bay of Bengal, ease rain deficit in State
points: The Regional Meteorological Centre has so far forecast moderate rainfall over southern districts till November 15, with rainfall likely to shift to north Tamil Nadu next week.
November is the wettest month of the year for many districts, including Chennai, Nagapattinam, Cuddalore and Tiruchi, which receive their maximum share of annual rainfall during this time.
This Northeast monsoon, districts like Cuddalore, Mayiladuthurai, Thanjavur, Chengalpattu and Tiruvarur, are among the districts that continue to record a rainfall deficit.

The weather agency has said an upper air cyclonic circulation over south Andaman Sea and neighbourhood is expected to trigger the formation of a low pressure area over southeast Bay of Bengal on Friday.
It is further likely to gather strength as depression by November 15.
V.R.Durai, Head, Regional Weather Forecasting Centre, RMC, said the weather agency is monitoring for chances of the system becoming a cyclone and the prospects of rainfall over TN.
“Normally, the weather systems that form over southwest Bay of Bengal have a tendency to move towards Tamil Nadu.

points: Christian organisations demanded police open rowdy sheets against those involved in the recent alleged assault on two young women in Meerpet and ensure accountability for the incident.
The demand was among a set of resolutions passed at a joint meeting convened by the Telangana United Christians and Pastors Association and Telangana United Christian Synod at MB Church.
The meeting was attended by bishops, pastors and representatives of various denominations.
The meeting also discussed long-pending community welfare issues.

They also sought a monthly honorarium for Below Poverty Line pastors on par with religious heads of other faiths.
The organisations expressed hope that the government would fulfil these demands as a Christmas gift this year.

items.title: APSCHE launches digital portal for accessible, self-paced learning
points: The Andhra Pradesh State Council of Higher Education (APSCHE) has launched ‘Vidya Vahini’, a digital learning portal that aims at providing accessible, flexible and quality-assured online learning opportunities for students and the faculty across higher…

The APSCHE LMS–MOOCs (Learning Management System-Massive Open Online Courses) platform enables learners to undertake courses at their own pace while complementing classroom teaching with high-quality digital content.

Students can register on the platform, browse the available course catalogue, enrol in relevant MOOCs, access learning materials, participate in assessments and track their progress towards successful course completion and certification, said an official…

The platform will benefit students by providing opportunities for self-paced and interdisciplinary learning, skill enhancement, emerging technology education and continuous academic enrichment beyond the conventional classroom environment.

items.title: Depression over Bay of Bengal likely by November 15: IMD
points: The India Meteorological Department (IMD), Amaravati, has said that the low-pressure area, which is likely to form over south-east Bay of Bengal around November 13, may intensify into a depression.

In a bulletin on Wednesday, the IMD said an upper air cyclonic circulation has formed over South Andaman Sea on Wednesday, and under its influence, a low-pressure area is likely to form over south-east Bay of Bengal.
It is-likely to become a well-marked low-pressure area around November 14 and intensify into a depression by November 15.
The IMD has not yet issued any rainfall alerts for the State.

Even as reports about another cyclonic storm are doing the rounds, weather experts at the IMD have said the system has to be tracked and that there may not be a possibility of formation of another cyclone.

points: Aluminum buyers on the London Metal Exchange are facing the most severe squeeze in decades as inventories backing contracts plunge and much of the remaining stock comes under the control of just two traders.

Spot prices for the crucial industrial metal spiked to trade $151 a ton above benchmark three-month futures on the exchange on Wednesday, hitting the highest level on record in data spanning more than 30 years.
The spread was trading at a discount as recently as mid-October, but it has corkscrewed higher as stockpiles in LME warehouses have plunged to the lowest level since 1990.

items.title: Bride-to-be, cousin killed as speeding lorry runs over scooter near Deepanjali Metro station
points: A family in Nagamangala taluk of Mandya district, which was preparing for a wedding scheduled for next Monday, was plunged into mourning after a bride-to-be and her cousin were killed in a road accident near Deepanjali Metro Station on Mysuru Road on…
The deceased have been identified as Sindhushree, an employee of a private firm, and her cousin Vidya, 19, a college student.
Sindhushree was scheduled to marry on November 16, with a reception planned for Sunday.
According to the police, the two women had left their native Aithanahalli village in Nagamangala taluk on a scooter to distribute wedding invitation cards among relatives.
At around 3.30 pm, when they were passing near Deepanjali Metro station, a speeding lorry rammed into their scooter.
Personnel from the Byatarayanapura Traffic Police Station rushed to the spot, seized the lorry and shifted the bodies for post-mortem examination.
A case has been registered at the Byatarayanapura Traffic Police Station, and efforts are under way to trace the absconding driver.

The incident is said to have taken place between Kacheri Chowk and Guru Ravidas Chowk.
The youths reportedly took the policeman to the District Police Headquarters after the alleged recovery.
Following the circulation of the video, Barnala Police initiated an inquiry and registered a case after verifying the footage.

items.title: Multibagger Cupid to be in focus on Thursday after Q2 net profit more than doubles to ₹56 crore; raises FY27 guidance
points: Multibagger Cupid shares are likely to be on investors' radar on Thursday, 12 November, as the company posted another solid quarter, led by consumer healthcare and FMCG business.
The company posted a 133% year-on-year jump in Q2 FY27 net profit to ₹56.22 crore, compared with ₹24.13 crore in the year-ago period.
For the first half of FY27, net profit surged 156% YoY to ₹100.37 crore from ₹39.14 crore in H1 FY26.
Revenue from operations grew 122% YoY to ₹187.86 crore in Q2 FY27 and 137% to ₹342.58 crore in H1 FY27.
The Consumer Healthcare & FMCG segment alone contributed ₹166.88 crore, representing 49% of sales, highlighting the increasing scale of its consumer portfolio.

Meanwhile, the international business contributed ₹112.73 crore, or 33% of H1 FY27 sales, supported by institutional demand through the PFSCM agreement and supplies under South Africa's 2025–30 national programme.

The woman claimed that when she called the cab driver to tell him about her pickup location, the man, instead of answering, asked her for sex.

items.title: Earthquake Of Magnitude 3.9 Strikes Shimla, No Damage Reported
points: An earthquake of magnitude 3.9 struck Himachal Pradesh's Shimla district on Wednesday night, with tremors felt in Jubbal and Rohru areas.
No loss of life or damage has been reported so far, officials said.
According to the National Centre for Seismology, the earthquake struck around 9.50 pm at a depth of 10 km.
Tremors lasting a few seconds were felt in Jubbal and Rohru, around 90-110 km from the state capital, reports reaching here said.
The epicentre was located in Shimla district at 31.118 degrees north latitude and 78.00 degrees east longitude.
The State Disaster Management Authority said there were no reports of damage in Shimla district or adjoining areas.
Himachal Pradesh falls in highly sensitive seismic zones IV and V.
A few months ago, the Bureau of Indian Standards proposed a new seismic map categorising the entire state under high-risk Zone VI.

items.title: Terrorists Opened Fire In Kulgam. How Alert CRPF Jawan Averted A Tragedy
points: The terror attack on a CRPF check post in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam district could have been a major tragedy if one of its personnel, who himself was injured, hadn't swiftly counter-fired, forcing the opponents to make a hasty retreat.
CCTV footage shows terrorists firing a barrage of bullets at CRPF troopers before the apparently well-planned attack was foiled.
At least two terrorists took cover behind a gabion structure, opened fire and managed to escape after their attempts were responded to.

Official sources say a prior intelligence alert about a suspected terrorist movement and the swift retaliatory action by a CRPF jawan "helped security forces thwart what could have been a major attack aimed at inflicting heavy casualties".
A CRPF camp is located less than 100 metres from the attack site.
The Kulgam attack comes against the backdrop of an extended period of relative calm in the Valley.

items.title: Hapag-Lloyd further raises its earnings outlook for the current financial year
points: Supported by continued robust spot freight rates, business performance in the fourth quarter is developing better than previously expected.

Group EBITDA is now expected to be in the range of USD 4.6 to 5.0 billion (previously: USD 3.9 to 4.4 billion) and Group EBIT in the range of USD 2.0 to 2.4 billion (previously: USD 1.25 to 1.75 billion).

items.title: French-speaking countries strengthen readiness for upcoming IMO audit cycle
points: Maritime administrations from 13 French-speaking countries are enhancing their preparedness for the next audit cycle under the IMO Member State Audit Scheme (IMSAS).
Preparing for the second audit cycle Ahead of the commencement of the second audit cycle in July 2027, the workshop is based on the revised Framework and Procedures for IMSAS (resolution A.1211(34)).
Participants are examining key changes to the audit process, including the introduction of the IMO Continuous Monitoring Mechanism (ICMM) and a risk-based approach to audit prioritization.
The training also focuses on the practical and administrative arrangements required for effective audit preparation and implementation.

Topics include the Audit Standard (III Code), the Memorandum of Cooperation (MoC), the State Audit Questionnaire (SAQ), the Verification Index, and gap analysis using the Non-exhaustive List of Obligations (resolution A.1208(34)).

By strengthening national capacities and promoting continuous improvement, the workshop supports sustained compliance with applicable IMO instruments and enhances Member States’ ability to meet their international obligations.

items.title: Rough weather disrupts bunkering in Gibraltar Strait and wider region

items.title: US 30-Year Mortgage Rates Fall for 4th Week
points: The average rate on a 30-year fixed US mortgage fell 9 basis points to 7.21% in the week ending November 6, marking a fourth consecutive weekly decline and providing some relief to the struggling housing market.
Borrowing costs have dropped nearly 30 basis points from an almost two-year high of 7.5% reached early last month, although rates remain elevated enough to deter many prospective buyers.
Lower financing costs helped drive a 7.5% increase in mortgage applications for home purchases, the largest weekly gain since mid-April and only the second rise since late August.
Applications for refinancing also increased 4.5%, extending their advance to a third consecutive week, although the index remains near its lowest level since January 2025.
Despite these improvements, a sustained decline in borrowing costs may be necessary to encourage stronger housing activity.
Contract signings for previously owned homes fell to a record low in September following a sharp rise in mortgage rates.

Considering the wider belt spanning Chittoor, Tirupati, Annamayya, and Kadapa, Totapuri cultivation stretches across nearly 90,000 hectares, with close to 50,000 farmers involved and producing an estimated 9 lakh tonnes every year.

The major mago growing hubs include Bangarupalem, Puthalapattu, Aragonda, Thavanampalle, Puttur, and Palamaner in Chittoor district; Rayachoti and Rajampet in Annamayya district, and Railway Koduru in Tirupati district respectively.

India cuts visa categories from 13 to 9, application form fields reduced by up to 70%
points: The Centre has reduced the number of main Indian visa categories from 13 to nine and sub-categories from 49 to 23, aimed at simplifying the country's visa regime, the ministry of home affairs said in a statement on Wednesday.
In a separate exercise, the Union home ministry is also moving to simplify visa application forms, reducing the number of fields by 65-70% across all 23 visa sub-categories.

The nine primary categories under India's visa regime now include – Business Visa, Diplomatic Visa, Work Visa, Journalist Visa, MedicaL Visa, Official Visa, Student Visa, Visitor Visa and Miscellaneous Visa.
B-1 Visa covers long-term, licence-based business activities, including foreign nationals seeking to establish industrial or business ventures in India.
B-2 Visa covers short-term, contract-based business activities, including Production Investment Business, conferences, sports, performative arts and films.
As part of the changes, the Student Visa category has also been consolidated into two sub-categories – S-1 and S-2.

items.title: Maersk hit by fresh cyber breach
points: Danish shipping giant AP Moller-Maersk has confirmed another cybersecurity breach after hackers gained access to an older IT system and extracted data, nearly a decade after the devastating NotPetya attack that cost the company up to $300m.
The Copenhagen-headquartered group said on Wednesday that the incident involved a local legacy system inherited through a previous acquisition.

Maersk’s cybersecurity team launched an investigation after discovering the intrusion and has taken steps to secure the affected system.”Our findings so far strongly suggest no sensitive data has been disclosed,” the company said.

The carrier said the breach appeared to be confined to the legacy system, with no indication that other Maersk systems or those belonging to customers and partners connected through APIs and electronic data interchange (EDI) had been compromised.

The announcement follows separate claims by a hacker group calling itself WhiteArmor that it had obtained around 100 GB of logistics data from a platform associated with LF Logistics, the Hong Kong-based logistics business Maersk acquired for $3.6bn in 2022.

items.title: Flex LNG lines up $145.5m leaseback
points: John Fredriksen-controlled Flex LNG has signed a $145.5m sale-and-leaseback deal for one of its LNG carriers, extending a fleet refinancing programme expected to release another $34m in cash.
The New York-listed owner disclosed the agreement with an unnamed Asian leasing company in its third-quarter update.
The deal covers the 2018-built, 173,400 cu m Flex Enterprise, which will be sold to the lessor and chartered back on a bareboat basis for approximately six years.
The financing carries an age-adjusted repayment profile of around 21 years and includes an option for Flex to repurchase the vessel at a fixed price after roughly six years.
Flex said it intends to use the proceeds to repay the outstanding balance on its existing $150m Flex Enterprise financing facility, which matures in June 2029.
Once the existing debt has been cleared, the company expects the refinancing to release approximately $34m in net cash.
The latest deal comes after Flex renegotiated the terms of an existing $330m sale-and-leaseback covering Flex Artemis and Flex Amber in October.

items.title: Volare snaps up $210m VLCC in Trafigura-linked deal
points: Trafigura-backed tanker owner Volare Shipping has agreed to acquire a VLCC newbuilding from an affiliate of its controlling shareholder for $210m, adding another supertanker to its expanding fleet just weeks after its Oslo market debut.
The Euronext Growth-listed company said it had struck a deal for the scrubber-fitted Veni Vidi Vici, which is currently undergoing sea trials at Hengli Heavy Industry in China.
The seller is an affiliate of Trafigura Maritime Logistics, Volare’s indirect majority shareholder.
The transaction is expected to close this month, subject to financing and customary conditions.
The acquisition will take Volare’s operating fleet to seven modern VLCCs, with another eight newbuildings scheduled to join through 2028.
The Singapore-incorporated company was launched by Trafigura in September and subsequently raised $500m in an Oslo private placement.
It entered the market with six trading VLCCs and eight newbuildings, with Trafigura retaining majority control and commercial management.

items.title: Canada puts Iranian tanker giant back under sanctions
points: Canada has reinstated sanctions against the National Iranian Tanker Company (NITC), reversing relief granted a decade ago under the international nuclear agreement with Tehran.
The move forms part of a package targeting 11 Iranian entities, including National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC), oil trading group Naftiran Intertrade and several major financial institutions.
The measures were announced by Canadian foreign minister Anita Anand during a G7 foreign ministers’ meeting in Paris.
The restrictions prohibit specified dealings involving the property of sanctioned entities and related financial services by people and businesses in Canada, as well as Canadians operating abroad.

The decision puts NITC back under Canadian restrictions for the first time since February 2016, when Ottawa removed the company and several other Iranian organisations from its sanctions list following implementation of the nuclear agreement.
NITC is one of the world’s major crude tanker operators and a central player in Iran’s seaborne oil exports.

Yangzijiang Maritime has separately announced orders for seven 114,000 dwt LR2 tankers at Chinese yards, also scheduled for delivery in 2029 and 2030.
Torm chief executive Jacob Meldgaard told analysts last week that the company had been discussing potential cooperation with its joint venture partner for some time.

Under the arrangement, Torm will retain full technical and commercial control of the vessels through its integrated One Torm platform once they enter service, with the two partners sharing the financial returns.

items.title: Panama Canal Raises Daily Transit Capacity as Water Conditions Improve

The adjustment adds one daily booking slot for Super vessels at the Panamax locks, increasing availability in that category from 18 to 19.
Total daily reservation capacity rises from 33 to 34 slots, including 24 at the Panamax locks and 10 at the larger Neopanamax locks.

items.title: ARAI Developing New Hydrogen Truck Engine And Testing Standards: Details
points: The Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) is working with the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) to develop a hydrogen-powered engine (H2-ICE) for heavy trucks and standardise the tests used to evaluate hydrogen vehicles.
The work focuses on a direct-injection hydrogen internal combustion engine, while the testing programme also covers vehicles that use hydrogen fuel cells.
The initiative was reported by Mint, citing people familiar with the project and ARAI's FY2026 annual report.
The programme forms part of the wider National Green Hydrogen Mission, which was approved in 2023 with an outlay of Rs 19,744 crore.
A hydrogen internal combustion engine, or H2-ICE, burns hydrogen inside engine cylinders to produce power.
ARAI is preparing testing protocols for both H2-ICE and hydrogen fuel-cell vehicles.
